newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada attracts record high 1996 travelers.
newsitem.headline: Canada attracts record high 1996 travelers.

text.p: Foreigners from the United States and overseas made a record 17.3 million overnight trips to Canada in 1996, injecting an unprecedented C$9.6 billion into the Canadian economy, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.

The rise in overseas travelers -- visitors from countries other than the United States -- rose to a record 4.4 million overnight trips, up 11.5 percent from a year earlier and the fifth consecutive annual increase, the federal agency said. Much of the growth stemmed from visits from Asia.
Overseas visitors injected C$4.5 billion into the Canadian economy, the agency said.

In 1996, more than half of the overnight trips overseas residents made to Canada were for holidays and recreation. One trip in four was to visit firends and relatives and one in seven was for business, StatsCan said. The proportions were relatively unchanged from 1995.
